title: Organizing Data in a Frequency Distribution Table
seo_title: Grade 7 Frequency Distribution Tables Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Organize statistical data in a frequency distribution table.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 frequency distribution table worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: tallies, frequencies, classes, class width, class marks and grouped data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The frequencies add up to the number of data values.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A frequency distribution table shows each value or class and how many times it occurs (its frequency).
  • Use tally marks to count, then write the frequency. The frequencies add up to the number of data values.
  • For many different values, group them into classes of equal width, like 50–59, 60–69. The class width is the difference between the lower limits: 60 − 50 = 10.
  • The class mark is the midpoint of a class: (50 + 59) ÷ 2 = 54.5.

Examples

Example

Classes 41–45, 46–50, 51–55

46 − 41 = 5

(41 + 45) ÷ 2 = 43

Answer: width 5, first class mark 43

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting twiceCross out each value as you tally it.
Width = upper − lower45 − 41 = 4, but the width is 5.
Boundary values50 belongs to 46–50, not 51–55.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 7 ask about frequency tables?
faq.a: Organize statistical data in a frequency distribution table.

faq.q: How many classes should I use?
faq.a: Usually 5 to 10 classes of equal width.

faq.q: What is a class mark used for?
faq.a: It stands for all the values in the class, for example to estimate the mean.
The frequency divided by the total.

sets.title: Classes, class width and class marks

items.q: A frequency table has the classes 10–14, 15–19, 20–24. What is the class width (class size)?
items.e: From one lower limit to the next: 15 − 10 = 5.

items.q: Scores are grouped in classes 40–49, 50–59, 60–69, … In which class is a score of 77?
items.e: 77 is from 70 to 79, so it is in the class 70–79.

items.q: What is the class mark (midpoint) of the class 55–59?
